requirements.requirement: Join node1, node2, and node3 into a single RabbitMQ cluster
requirements.summary: rabbitmqctl cluster_status on node1 after join_cluster on node2 and node3 shows all three nodes as disc nodes and all three listed as running_nodes with no partitions, confirming a functioning single cluster.
add_vhost payments succeeded and list_vhosts on node1 confirms both / and payments exist.

requirements.requirement: Create an application account that can publish and consume on the payments vhost
requirements.summary: User app_payments was created with full configure/write/read permissions (.*/.*/.*) scoped to the payments vhost, and a Python/pika publish test against that vhost using the app credentials succeeded (publish_confirmed). A consumer script (rmq_consume_one.py) was written to node1/node2/node3 but the captured command timeline ends (due to executor timeout) before any consume invocation is shown, so successful consumption by the app account is not directly demonstrated.

requirements.requirement: Messages published to a durable queue must survive the loss of any one node and remain consumable from the remaining nodes
requirements.summary: An ha-all mirroring policy (ha-mode=all, ha-sync-mode=automatic) was applied to the payments vhost, and after publishing a durable message to the 'orders' queue, list_queues shows the message mirrored with synchronised_slave_pids on both node2 and node3 -- strong supporting configuration evidence. However, no captured command stops or removes a node (e.g. rabbitmqctl stop_app / node shutdown) to directly observe the queue and message surviving a node loss and remaining consumable from the survivors; the timeline ends at the mirror-status check before any disruption test.

overall_summary: The executor successfully installed RabbitMQ 3.5.7 on all three Ubuntu 16.04 nodes, joined them into a single cluster (confirmed via cluster_status), created the payments vhost, created an app_payments user scoped to that vhost, applied an ha-all mirroring policy, and confirmed a durable message was published and mirrored/synchronised to both other nodes. However, the run was cut off by a 2100-second timeout (lifecycle_outcome: executor_timed_out) before any consume test or an actual node-loss/failover test could be captured, so the core resiliency requirement and the full publish-and-consume requirement are only partially demonstrated via configuration and partial testing rather than an end-to-end observed transition.
limitations: No captured command stops rabbitmq on any node, kills a node's app, or otherwise simulates node loss to directly verify message survival and consumption from the remaining nodes; only supporting mirror-policy configuration and slave-sync status are available.
No captured command exercises the deployed rmq_consume_one.py consumer script to prove the app_payments account can actually consume messages; only the publish path was exercised.
The executor's own final report is empty/blocked (timeout) and contributes no evidence beyond the raw command timeline.

Boot-identity observations for all three nodes are identical between before_prepare and after_executor, indicating no OS reboot/restart evidence protocol was executed for any node; this is expected given the timeout but is a gap if provider-wide restart evidence was otherwise expected.

operational_hygiene.summary: Executor commands were mostly diagnostic/config/test in service of the task: apt-get installs of rabbitmq-server (interrupted once by a proxy timeout, requiring a pkill/dpkg --configure -a recovery on node2, which was a reasonable corrective action, not a new unnecessary mutation), erlang cookie sync across nodes, cluster join, vhost/user/policy setup, management plugin enable, and pip/pika installs to build a functional test harness. A rabbitmqadmin CLI binary was downloaded to node1 (cmd-eae5d887e34046bf) but abandoned in favor of a Python/pika script after an access-refused error; it was left in place (/usr/local/bin/rabbitmqadmin) as low-risk, bounded residue. Several install/log/test-script temp files (/tmp/install.log, /tmp/install2.log, /tmp/pika_install*.log, /tmp/rmq_declare_publish.py, /tmp/rmq_consume_one.py) remained on all three nodes per the after-executor temp-file diff -- unremoved residue, but consistent with the run being cut short by the timeout rather than intentional carelessness. No failed services, unsafe exposure, or destructive actions were observed.
